messages:
Alerts Bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT detected — p99 latency breach for cohort 'dedicated-hotshot-us-east' (streaming). auto-threshold crossed at 2026-03-15T12:34:10Z. p95 ~ 1.2s -> 5.8s, p99 ~ 2.9s -> 21s.
Oncall Bot: paging Emma L (oncall). runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/dedicated-warmup
Emma L: I'm on it. Affected route(s)?
Raj P: seeing sustained queue_depth spikes on hotshot pool: `queue_depth=1243` across clients. Lots of long lived streaming sessions not progressing.
Sophie K: logs show warmup handshake delays — warmup tasks sit at state=ALLOCATED but never finish:
```
warmup: slot=slot-34 state=ALLOCATED handshake=STARTED elapsed=00:00:42
worker: recv handshake timeout after 45s
kv_cache: cold_miss=true
```
Tom R: autoscaler telemetry indicates scale requests were issued but slot registration lagged. kube events show image pull & nfs mount blips around the same time.
Maria S: customer impact: two enterprise customers seeing retries and 30% higher tail latency, one reported streaming stalls in prod. They filed PSC ticket #2026-0342.
Emma L: immediate mitigations: 1) open manual scale to bypass autoscaler, 2) enable fallback routing to smaller model variant in region, 3) increase warmup parallelism. Who can run manual scale?
Raj P: I can. Running temporary scale: `rbctl pool scale --pool hotshot-us-east --count 8 --reason "incident 4444444444 manual scale"`
Infra Pager: action: manual scale started by Raj P at 12:38Z.
Sophie K: while scaling, we should unblock warmup. Suspect NFS mount latency causing worker startup to stall warmup. Checking node logs.
Tom R: found repeated mount timeouts: `mount.nfs: server 10.0.12.5 not responding, timed out` across new nodes. Mount retries tied to warmup failures.
Emma L: OK, plan: (A) route new requests to fallback pool in eu-west while warmup completes, (B) increase autoscaler warmup timeout to give more time for slot registration, (C) disable NFS mounting for warmup path on new nodes and use local tmpfs as workaround.
Maria S: notify affected customers with a short status update: ETA 15-30m for mitigation. I'll draft.
Raj P: manual scale completed, 6 -> 8 nodes, but warmup still flapping on 2 nodes due to mount failures.
Sophie K: kicking a manual warmup job on each new node: `rbctl warmup --node node-87 --profile hotshot --blocking` — running now.
Emma L: streaming stalls look correlated with a specific SDK handshake pattern that triggers a long prefix cache miss; we're seeing many concurrent cache misses because of a burst from an onboarding job (customer onboarding bulk ingest).
Tom R: confirmed — ingestion service started a fan-out of streaming sessions at 12:30Z. That created many cold KV contexts which multiplied warmup work.
Infra Pager: work item: throttle onboarding job or queue it. Can service team pause that job?
Sophie K: pinging @dev-onboarding.
Emma L: temporary policy: apply request rate-limit on onboarding token and route their traffic to best-effort pool until warmup finishes.
Maria S: customer comms: "We're mitigating a latency incident impacting streaming responses for dedicated pools in us-east. We've applied throttles and scaled capacity; engineers are resolving warmup registration failures. Expect improvements within 20-30 minutes. We'll follow up once resolved." Would you like me to send now? :email:
Emma L: yes, send now. Keep updates every 15 minutes or on milestone changes.
Raj P: patching autoscaler: bump `warmup_timeout` from 30s -> 90s for hotshot pools to reduce premature failures. Deploying now via `deploy/autoscaler/hotshot-config`
Sophie K: warmup jobs now succeeding on nodes that used tmpfs workaround — handshake completes in ~6-12s. Streaming stalls subsiding. p99 trending down: 21s -> 9.5s.
Tom R: still seeing ~3% of sessions that never progress and end with `ERR_STREAM_STALLED`. Capturing stack traces.
Emma L: root cause hypothesis: combined effect of (1) onboarding fan-out generating high concurrent cold KV contexts, (2) NFS mount timeouts delaying container start/warmup, (3) autoscaler warmup timeout too short leading to scale churn and capacity oscillation.
Maria S: incident severity: P1 -> keeping pager escalation. CS notified.
Infra Pager: temp mitigations summary (for postmortem): `manual scale +8 nodes`, `autoscaler warmup_timeout increased`, `tmpfs warmup path enabled`, `onboarding job throttled`, `fallback routing enabled`.
Raj P: metrics now: queue_depth 1243 -> 210 -> 45 over 22 minutes. p95 ~ 1.8s, p99 ~ 6.2s.
Emma L: preparing oncall handoff at top of the hour. If stable for 20m, downgrade to P2.
Sophie K: will follow up with detailed logs and a temp dashboard showing node warmup success rates.
Tom R: collecting `kubectl describe` dump and node kubelet logs; dropping into #eng-infra for deeper investigation.
Maria S: customer update posted to PSC and status page.
Oncall Bot: oncall handoff scheduled: Emma L -> Raj P at 13:00Z.
Emma L: handing off to Raj P. Key follow-ups: verify warmup reliability with tmpfs change, drive root cause on NFS timeouts, confirm autoscaler behavior under burst. If anything regresses, re-escalate.
Raj P: ack. I'll coordinate with dev-onboarding and infra to reproduce in staging and validate fix for NFS mount timeouts.
Sophie K: adding link to raw logs: https://logs.internal/streams/4444444444 (scrubbed).
Emma L: closing incident when p99 < 3s and queue_depth < 50 for 30 consecutive minutes.
Maria S: thanks team. I'll start postmortem doc and customer RCA draft.
Oncall Bot: INCIDENT update: mitigations applied; monitoring.
Alerts Bot: auto-resolve check in 40m if metrics stable.
Emma L: typing final note before handoff: great cross-team response. main lessons: tune warmup timeouts, avoid NFS for critical warmup path, rate-limit large fan-outs.
